description: prometheus-s3-exporter 6.x: one exporter for many buckets, or one per bucket -- the dashboard reads the same in both. Buckets are keyed by (bucket_namespace, name). Sections: buckets, the problems among them, the endpoints they live on (DNS, TCP, TLS), the exporters themselves (per pod), and their logs.
title: S3 buckets - prometheus-s3-exporter

panels.description: Buckets whose credentials were read and that are probed, across every exporter.
panels.title: Buckets watched

panels.description: Buckets in a configuration whose credentials cannot be read: a missing Secret, key or RoleBinding. See the Not watched table and the logs.
panels.title: Not watched

panels.description: Endpoints whose last check failed in at least one exporter: DNS, TCP or TLS.
panels.title: Endpoints down

panels.description: Collections late with no worker free: raise max_concurrent_collections or the CPU limit.
panels.title: Collections overdue

panels.description: Exporters whose last collector.yml content was rejected: the previous configuration is in force.
panels.title: Config rejected

panels.description: Exporters whose collector.yml changed a setting that only a restart applies.
panels.title: Restart required

panels.description: Time left on the endpoint certificate closest to its end. The exporter warns in its log under 14 days.
panels.title: Nearest cert expiry

panels.description: One row per watched bucket, keyed by namespace and name, whichever exporter watches it. Unreachable buckets first. Errors/h and Main error come from the probe's attempts, retried ones included; Connections/h counts the probe's reconnections (one every probe means the idle timeout in front of the storage is shorter than connectivity_interval). Interval is the one in force: stretched to four times the collection time for slow buckets. A probe-only bucket has no size.
panels.title: Buckets

panels.description: Buckets listed in a configuration whose credentials cannot be read yet. The exporter reads the Secret again every credentials_refresh seconds and picks the bucket up once it is fixed; the reason is in its log and in /readyz. Empty when every bucket is watched.
panels.title: Not watched

panels.description: Only the buckets whose probe failed at least once in the time range: with a hundred buckets, the green ones say nothing.

targets.expr:
max by (bucket_namespace, name) (webtech_s3_bucket_reachable{bucket_namespace=~"$namespace", name=~"$bucket"})
  and on (bucket_namespace, name)
    (min by (bucket_namespace, name) (min_over_time(webtech_s3_bucket_reachable{bucket_namespace=~"$namespace", name=~"$bucket"}[$__range] @ end())) == 0)

panels.title: Reachability of the buckets that failed
Slowest probes (top 10)
panels.description: The ten buckets with the slowest probe at each moment. Steps in multiples of 5s on a new connection point at lost DNS queries; see the endpoints.

panels.title: Probe errors by reason
panels.description: Failed probe attempts, retried ones included, by where they failed: dns, connect_timeout, connect, read_timeout, http_5xx, http_4xx.

panels.title: Largest buckets (top 10)
panels.description: Size of the ten largest buckets in the selection.

panels.title: Slowest collections (top 10)
panels.description: Duration of the last collection of the ten slowest buckets. With the list source it grows with the object count, and the interval in force stretches to four times it.

Each endpoint checked once per exporter, whatever the number of buckets on it: its name resolved, a TCP connection, a TLS handshake for https. Up is the worst of the exporters that check it. A DNS failure here while the buckets stay reachable is a DNS outage their open connections hide.
panels.title: Endpoints
Endpoint: DNS, TCP, TLS
panels.description: Each endpoint checked on its own every probe interval: its name resolved through the pod's resolver (search list and ndots included), a TCP connection, a TLS handshake for https. Steps at multiples of 5s in dns are lost DNS queries waiting out the resolver's timeout; bars are failed checks, by the phase that failed.

One row per exporter pod. CPU, Memory and Throttled come from cAdvisor, joined on (namespace, pod): they need a datasource that sees both the container metrics and the exporters, i.e. Thanos Querier rather than the user-workload Prometheus alone. A hundred buckets take about 160 MB; Throttled above a few percent slows the listings, not the probes.

targets.expr: max by (pod) (sum by (namespace, pod) (rate(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total{container!="", container!="POD"}[5m])) * 1000 and on (namespace, pod) webtech_s3_exporter_up)
max by (pod) (sum by (namespace, pod) (container_memory_working_set_bytes{container!="", container!="POD"}) and on (namespace, pod) webtech_s3_exporter_up)

max by (pod) ((sum by (namespace, pod) (rate(container_cpu_cfs_throttled_periods_total[5m])) / sum by (namespace, pod) (rate(container_cpu_cfs_periods_total[5m]))) and on (namespace, pod) webtech_s3_exporter_up)

panels.title: Exporters

panels.description: The exporters' own account: a bucket lost and found again, with every attempt and its root cause; an endpoint failing at dns, tcp or tls; a change of address; a certificate close to its end; a configuration reloaded or rejected; a Secret that cannot be read. Set the log selector variable to where the exporters' logs live.

targets.expr: ${log_selector} |~ "became unreachable|is reachable again|Endpoint .* failed at|resolves to|certificate of|Configuration|restart the exporter|is not watched|Cannot read|now names bucket|Bucket .* (added|removed|changed)"

panels.title: Events

list.description: LogQL stream selector for the exporters' logs. The default matches the local stack; on OpenShift use e.g. {namespace="my-ns", container="s3-exporter"}.
list.label: Log selector
list.name: log_selector
